name: Crossref_search_works
description: Search Crossref Works API for scholarly articles, publications, and research outputs by keyword. Returns metadata including title, abstract, journal, authors, publication year, DOI, URL, citations, and publisher. Supports filtering by publication type (journal article, conference paper, etc.) and date range. Use this to discover academic literature, verify citations, or build bibliographies. Find DOIs to use with Crossref_get_work for complete metadata. The response reports 'count' (works in this page) alongside 'total_count' (works matching the query in all of Crossref) -- these differ on almost every real search, since 'limit' defaults to 10 and caps at 100, so treat 'count' as a page size and never as the size of the literature. When they differ, 'truncated' is true and 'truncation_note' gives the 'offset' for the next page. Note: Crossref's own API weakens keyword relevance-matching whenever a non-default 'sort' query param is combined with 'query' (e.g. sort=is-referenced-by-count), returning globally top-cited works largely unrelated to the search term -- omit 'sort' (the default relevance ranking) unless you have separately verified the combination for your query. For deep paging past Crossref's offset cap, start with the default cursor='*' and, while metadata.has_more is true, pass metadata.next_cursor as cursor with the same query and filters (cursor and offset cannot be combined).

query.description: Search query for Crossref works. Use keywords separated by spaces to refine your search across titles, abstracts, authors, and other bibliographic fields.

limit.description: Number of articles to return in this page. This sets the maximum number of articles retrieved from Crossref. Max 100 per request. It does not change 'total_count', which always reports how many works match the query.

offset.description: Skip this many matching works before returning results. Use with 'limit' to page through a result set larger than 100; the response 'truncation_note' gives the offset for the next page.

filter.description: Optional filter string for Crossref API. Examples: 'type:journal-article' (only journal articles), 'from-pub-date:2020-01-01' (published after date), 'has-abstract:true' (only with abstracts). Multiple filters comma-separated.

cursor.description: Crossref deep-pagination cursor. Use '*' for the first page, then metadata.next_cursor.

ISSN.description: ISSNs of the container journal, e.g. ['0022-3913']. Print and electronic together, with no indication of which is which - issn-type below separates them.

URL.description: The work's canonical DOI URL, e.g. 'https://doi.org/10.1067/mpr.2000.110262'. The link to give a reader; the bare DOI is not one.

alternative-id.description: The publisher's own identifiers for the work, e.g. ['S002239130074011X'] - a PII here. How the work is found in the publisher's own system.

content-domain.description: Where the publisher asserts the content may be hosted - 'domain' and 'crossmark-restriction'. A restriction here means a copy elsewhere is not the publisher's version of record.

created.description: When the DOI record was first created as Crossref's structured date: 'date-parts' (a nested [[year, month, day]] array, where a month or day may simply be absent), plus 'date-time' and a unix 'timestamp' on most. The nesting is one level deeper than it looks - date-parts[0] is the date.

date-parts.description: [[year, month, day]], truncated where the precision is lower.

date-time.description: ISO 8601 form of the same date.

deposited.description: When the metadata was last deposited as Crossref's structured date: 'date-parts' (a nested [[year, month, day]] array, where a month or day may simply be absent), plus 'date-time' and a unix 'timestamp' on most. The nesting is one level deeper than it looks - date-parts[0] is the date.

date-time.description: ISO 8601 form of the same date.

indexed.description: When Crossref last indexed the record as Crossref's structured date: 'date-parts' (a nested [[year, month, day]] array, where a month or day may simply be absent), plus 'date-time' and a unix 'timestamp' on most. The nesting is one level deeper than it looks - date-parts[0] is the date.

date-time.description: ISO 8601 form of the same date.

issn-type.description: The same ISSNs typed, each {'value', 'type'} with type 'print' or 'electronic'. The only way to pick the right one for a lookup.

issued.description: The earliest publication date of any form as Crossref's structured date: 'date-parts' (a nested [[year, month, day]] array, where a month or day may simply be absent), plus 'date-time' and a unix 'timestamp' on most. The nesting is one level deeper than it looks - date-parts[0] is the date.

date-time.description: ISO 8601 form of the same date.

journal-issue.description: The issue the work belongs to, with its 'issue' number and 'published-print' date. The issue's own date, which can differ from the work's.

license.description: Licence terms, each with 'URL', 'content-version' ('vor', 'am', 'tdm'), 'start' and a delay. The content-version matters: a licence on the accepted manuscript does not cover the published version.

link.description: Full-text links, each with 'URL', 'content-type', 'content-version' and 'intended-application' ('text-mining' or 'similarity-checking'). A text-mining link is not a reader link and often needs an API key.

member.description: Crossref member id of the depositing publisher, e.g. '78'. A string, not a number.

page.description: Page range, e.g. '492-498'. Needed to cite the work at all.

prefix.description: The DOI's registrant prefix, e.g. '10.1067'. Identifies the publisher without parsing the DOI.

published-print.description: The print publication date as Crossref's structured date: 'date-parts' (a nested [[year, month, day]] array, where a month or day may simply be absent), plus 'date-time' and a unix 'timestamp' on most. The nesting is one level deeper than it looks - date-parts[0] is the date.

date-parts.description: [[year, month, day]], truncated where the precision is lower.

date-time.description: ISO 8601 form of the same date.

reference-count.description: How many references the work declares, e.g. 66.

references-count.description: The same count under Crossref's other spelling; both are returned and they agree. Declared so a caller reading one is not left wondering about the other.

resource.description: The primary resource, under 'primary' with its URL - where the DOI actually resolves to, which can differ from the doi.org link.

score.description: Relevance score for the hit, e.g. 5.1680684. Results are ordered by it, so without it a weak match cannot be told from a strong one and the ranking cannot be reproduced.

short-container-title.description: Abbreviated journal title, e.g. ['The Journal of Prosthetic Dentistry']. What a citation style abbreviates to.

name: Crossref_get_work
description: Get complete metadata for a specific scholarly work by its DOI (Digital Object Identifier). Returns comprehensive bibliographic information including title, abstract, full author list with affiliations and ORCIDs, journal details, publication dates, volume/issue/pages, references, citations, license, funding information, and related identifiers. Essential for verifying citations, extracting complete metadata, or building reference managers. DOIs can be found using Crossref_search_works (format: 10.####/...).

name: Crossref_get_journal
description: Get metadata for a specific journal by its ISSN (International Standard Serial Number). Returns journal details including title, publisher, ISSN variants (print/electronic), coverage dates, and publication frequency. Use this to verify journal information, assess journal credibility for submissions, check publisher details, or validate ISSNs. Find ISSNs from publication metadata or journal databases (format: ####-####).

issn.description: Journal ISSN in format ####-#### (e.g., '1476-4687' for Nature, '1932-6203' for PLOS ONE). Both print and electronic ISSNs are accepted.

issn-type.description: The same ISSNs typed, each {'value', 'type'} with type 'print' or 'electronic'. The only way to pick the right one for a lookup.

coverage-type.description: Metadata coverage split by record type, each {all, backfile, current} -- the fraction of the journal's deposits carrying each metadata element. Coverage, not counts.

last-status-check-time.description: When Crossref last checked the journal's status, a UNIX epoch MILLISECOND count, e.g. 1794337639505. Divide by 1000 before converting.

name: Crossref_list_funders
description: Search and list research funding organizations in the Crossref database. Returns funder details including funder ID, name, location, DOI count, and alternative names. Use this to discover funder identifiers for filtering publications by funding source, or to explore research funding patterns. Essential for grant analysis, funding compliance, or finding publications funded by specific organizations (e.g., NIH, NSF, ERC). The response reports 'count' (funders in this page) alongside 'total_count' (funders matching the query in all of Crossref); 'limit' defaults to 20, so treat 'count' as a page size. When they differ, 'truncated' is true and 'truncation_note' gives the 'offset' for the next page. For deep paging, start with cursor='*' and continue with metadata.next_cursor while metadata.has_more is true (cursor and offset cannot be combined).

query.description: Search query for funder names (e.g., 'National Science Foundation', 'NIH', 'European Research Council', 'Wellcome Trust').

limit.description: Maximum number of funders to return in this page (default: 20, max: 100). It does not change 'total_count', which always reports how many funders match.

offset.description: Skip this many matching funders before returning results. Use with 'limit' to page through the full result set; the response 'truncation_note' gives the offset for the next page.

cursor.description: Crossref deep-pagination cursor. Use '*' initially, then metadata.next_cursor.

uri.description: The funder's canonical URI in the Crossref Funder Registry, e.g. 'https://doi.org/10.13039/501100001711'. This is the identifier to record for the funder; the numeric id alone does not resolve.

name: Crossref_get_funder
description: Get detailed metadata for a specific research funder by its Crossref funder ID. Returns comprehensive funder information including official name, alternative names, location, hierarchy (parent organizations), DOI count, and URI. Use this to understand funder details, verify funder identifiers, or explore funding relationships. Find funder IDs using Crossref_list_funders (format: numeric ID like '100000001' for NSF, '100000002' for NIH).

funder_id.description: Crossref funder identifier (e.g., '100000001' for NSF, '100000002' for NIH, '501100000780' for European Commission). Find IDs using Crossref_list_funders.

descendant-work-count.description: Works attributed to this funder OR any funder below it in the hierarchy, e.g. 569553. The larger of the two and the right one for 'how much did this agency fund'.

descendants.description: Funder ids below this one in the Crossref funder hierarchy, e.g. ['100000076', ...] (84 entries).

hierarchy-names.description: Map of funder id to name for the funders in this hierarchy, e.g. {'100000081': 'Directorate for Education and Human Resources', ...}. Keyed by id, so look names up rather than iterating positionally.

tokens.description: The funder's name broken into lowercase search tokens, e.g. ['national', 'science', 'foundation', ...] (21 entries). Crossref's own index terms, not a list of alternative names.

work-count.description: Works attributed to this funder itself, e.g. 463347.

name: Crossref_list_types
description: List all publication types available in Crossref (e.g., journal-article, book-chapter, conference-paper, dataset, preprint). Returns type identifiers and labels. Use this to discover valid publication type filters for Crossref_search_works, understand the classification of research outputs, or analyze publication type distributions. Essential for constructing precise search queries or filtering results by publication category.

name: Crossref_search_members
description: Search Crossref members (publishers / depositing organizations) by name. Returns each member's numeric Crossref member id, primary name, location, and DOI-coverage analytics: counts of current, backfile, and total DOIs, plus per-year DOI breakdowns and prefixes. Use this to find a publisher's member id (for Crossref_get_member), compare publisher output, or analyze DOI/journal coverage. Example: query 'plos' -> member id 340 'Public Library of Science (PLoS)'. The response reports 'count' (members in this page) alongside 'total_count' (members matching the query in all of Crossref) -- e.g. query 'university' matches 4032, far more than the default 'limit' of 20 returns -- so treat 'count' as a page size. When they differ, 'truncated' is true and 'truncation_note' gives the 'offset' for the next page. For deep paging, start with cursor='*' and continue with metadata.next_cursor while metadata.has_more is true (cursor and offset cannot be combined).

query.description: Publisher / member name to search (e.g., 'plos', 'elsevier', 'springer', 'wiley'). Prefer a single distinctive word: Crossref's own search can return zero results for multi-word brand names (e.g. 'springer nature' finds nothing even though 'springer' alone matches).

limit.description: Maximum number of members to return in this page. Max 100 per request. It does not change 'total_count', which always reports how many members match.

offset.description: Skip this many matching members before returning results. Use with 'limit' to page through the full result set; the response 'truncation_note' gives the offset for the next page.

cursor.description: Crossref deep-pagination cursor. Use '*' initially, then metadata.next_cursor.

return_schema.description: List of Crossref member (publisher) records matching the search query, each with DOI-coverage analytics.

prefix.description: The DOI's registrant prefix, e.g. '10.1067'. Identifies the publisher without parsing the DOI.

counts-type.description: Deposit counts split by record type, each {all, backfile, current}.

coverage-type.description: Metadata coverage split by record type, each {all, backfile, current} -- the fraction of deposits carrying each element.

last-status-check-time.description: When Crossref last checked the member's status, a UNIX epoch MILLISECOND count, e.g. 1794352273565.

names.description: Every name this member is known by, e.g. ['Public Library of Science (PLoS)', ...].

tokens.description: The member's names broken into lowercase search tokens, e.g. ['public', 'library', 'science', ...].

name: Crossref_get_member
description: Get a specific Crossref member (publisher) by its numeric member id, with full DOI-coverage analytics: primary name, location, counts of current/backfile/total DOIs, per-year DOI breakdowns (dois-by-issued-year), DOI prefixes, and deposit/coverage flags. Use this to audit a publisher's DOI output over time or verify member metadata. Find ids with Crossref_search_members. Example: member id 78 -> 'Elsevier BV', total-dois 24961410.

member_id.description: Numeric Crossref member id (e.g., '78' for Elsevier BV, '340' for PLOS). Find ids using Crossref_search_members.

oneOf.description: Crossref member (publisher) metadata with DOI-coverage analytics.

prefix.description: The DOI's registrant prefix, e.g. '10.1067'. Identifies the publisher without parsing the DOI.

counts-type.description: Deposit counts split by record type, each as {all, backfile, current}. 'current' is roughly the last two years, 'backfile' everything older.

coverage-type.description: Metadata coverage split by record type, each as {all, backfile, current}, giving the fraction of records carrying each metadata element. This is how complete the member's deposits are, not how many there are.

last-status-check-time.description: When Crossref last checked the member's status, as a UNIX epoch MILLISECOND count, e.g. 1794352239165 -- divide by 1000 before converting.

names.description: Every name the member is known by, e.g. ['Elsevier BV', ...] (33 entries). `primary-name` gives the main one.

tokens.description: The member's names broken into lowercase search tokens, e.g. ['elsevier'].
